title: Copper Beech: Ancient Purple Beeches You Can Visit
meta_description: Every copper beech descends from an accident: a mutation that loses to green beeches in the wild and survives because gardeners liked the colour.
intro: Every copper beech in Europe descends from an accident. The purple leaf is a mutation that turns up at random in wild green beech forests, and it is a handicap rather than an advantage: the pigment masks the chlorophyll underneath and cuts the light the leaf can put to work, so purple seedlings are outgrown by green ones and vanish. The tree exists in numbers only because gardeners in German and Swiss forests found the freak worth keeping and propagated it, and because it does not come true from seed it is usually grafted. Leiden's was grafted low onto a green rootstock, and two centuries of mismatched growth rates have left it with a broad gnarled base that looks nothing like a beech. Boston's is the only living Historic Landmark in Cambridge, designated in 1985 to stop a building. Eleven cities hold the thirteen mapped here, from Portland to Porto.
